summary: Intro discovery for PLG/self-serve Redwood API. Customer interested in fast time-to-first-token, free credits for evaluation, and evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for PII-sensitive workloads. Discussed quickstart, SDKs, demo apps, basic latency/cost tradeoffs, and next steps to run benchmarks and share security docs.
transcript: 00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood, i'm the ae on this account 00:04 Alex: hey maya thanks, alex here, CTO at sunrise ai, priya and jordan are with me 00:09 Maya: awesome, quick intros? 00:11 Priya: hi i'm priya, ml eng, will own the eval and integration 00:14 Jordan: jordan, infra, mainly network and security bits 00:17 Liam: liam here, se, i can run through quickstart and perf stuff 00:21 Maya: great, goal for today's call is to understand your eval needs, quickstart path, and whether hosted quickstart is sufficient or you need dedicated/private early on 00:30 Alex: briefly, we build a customer-facing assistant that touches PII, some PHI-like fields, so data residency and kms are important, but we want to move quickly. free credits and time-to-first-token matter a lot 00:44 Maya: totally makes sense. our PLG quickstart is designed for that — sign up, get free credits, sdk + example apps, and you can be at first token in under 10 minutes usually 00:56 Priya: under 10 minutes, nice. what's in the quickstart? 00:59 Liam: it includes an SDK, sample prompt sets, a small demo app, and a script to run a basic throughput/latency test. we also provide a workbook that maps model choices and quantization to expected latency and cost 01:12 Alex: question — with demo/test data going to hosted api will that persist? we need to be sure data retention for evaluation is minimal, and logs aren't retained beyond eval 01:22 Maya: good callout. hosted sandbox accounts have limited retention; by default logs are kept for 30 days, but for evals we can enable a stricter retention policy or sign a NDA to scrub sample data. i'll send the security doc that covers retention and audit logs 01:36 Jordan: and what about kms and sso? if we move to dedicated/private we need customer-managed kms and our sso provider (okta) 01:44 Liam: for dedicated we offer customer-managed KMS integration and SAML/SSO support; Private (VPC) offers a private control plane option and can be deployed into your VPC with HSM support if required. there are infra checklists we can share 01:56 Priya: sounds good. question on the hosted api — can we do a perf run to compare tokens/sec vs aoa? i mean vs other endpoints, like anthro and gpt 02:04 Maya: (laughs) vs anthro and gpt yes. we do have benchmark sheets that show sample throughput on common GPU types; we recommend running your own 1k request benchmark with your prompt set 02:10 Alex: what's the typical cost delta between hosted and dedicated? we expect to be high volume if the pilot goes well 02:17 Maya: hosted is pay-as-you-go on token units; dedicated is reserved capacity with lower unit costs but monthly commit. ballpark depends on model size and q config, but clients often see 25-60% cost reduction on per-token when moving to dedicated for sustained load 02:31 Priya: specifics matter — what about quantization options? do you support int8 / awq / q5? 02:36 Liam: we support a couple of quantization profiles; our runtime supports int8-like profiles and we have optimized kernels for awq/q5 families. we can recommend a profile per model and workload. i'll include recommended models + quant profiles in the spreadsheet 02:49 Jordan: network egress and VPC peering — if we do private, how is traffic routed, and do you support transit gateway or direct connect? 02:58 Liam: for private we typically set up VPC peering or a transit gateway, and we can integrate with your direct connect. there are bandwidth and egress cost considerations — we'll share the network topology doc 03:10 Alex: timeline wise, we want to run a 2-week pilot and have a go/no-go in 6 weeks. stakeholder list includes product, infra, and compliance 03:20 Maya: that timeline makes sense. typical flow: quickstart + creds + free credits (1 week), run bench + basic integration (week 2), then pilot on dedicated if warranted 03:29 Priya: about free credits — how much do you give and does it cover benchmark runs? 03:33 Maya: we give evaluation credits tied to account size, usually enough for a modest benchmark (couple thousand requests). for larger benchmark runs we can extend credits or run a co-run with an SE 03:43 Alex: can you do a co-run where liam helps run the large benchmark? 03:46 Liam: yes happy to do that. we can co-run and capture tracing, token-level latencies, and KV cache hit stats 03:54 Alex: you mentioned kv cache, do you mean K V cache? i think our previous vendor called it persistent context cache 03:59 Liam: yeah the caching is kv-style — prefix cache + session-level caching to save repeated tokens and improve tail latencies 04:07 Priya: any limits on session length? like how big can a cached context be? 04:11 Liam: we can configure max KV size per model; typical defaults are 64k tokens of KV state depending on model. for huge contexts we recommend segmented caching strategies 04:23 Alex: security questions — SOC 2 type II, iso, audit logs — do you have those certs? 04:28 Maya: redwood is SOC 2 compliant, and we have ISO docs for enterprises. i'll attach the cert PDF. audit logs are available in the console and can be exported 04:36 Jordan: can logs be sent to our SIEM? 04:39 Liam: yes we support log forwarding via syslog or cloudwatch, and can also provide structured traces for per-request debugging 04:46 Priya: curious about SLOs — for hosted do you publish latency percentile SLOs? 04:50 Maya: hosted has latency targets by model class, and dedicated comes with SLA-backed targets. console shows p50/p95/p99 traces by route 04:58 Alex: great. another question — what's the path to private on-prem? do you have a packaged appliance? 05:03 Liam: we have an on-prem package for air-gapped deployments; typically enterprise customers start on dedicated or hosted and then move to private on-prem if regulation demands it 05:12 Maya: for the quickstart we recommend starting hosted to move fast, then if pilot shows sustained usage we discuss dedicated reserve. private is heavier but doable for regulated workloads 05:22 Alex: ok makes sense. what about developer experience — do you have SDKs and first-party examples for node/python and dev tools? 05:27 Liam: yes official SDKs for node/python, plus sample apps and a postman collection. time-to-first-token for a typical engineer is ~10 minutes from signup 05:36 Priya: are there rate limits on the free credits account? 05:39 Maya: sandbox accounts have soft rate limits to prevent abuse but they're generous enough for dev/proof-of-concept. we can lift limits for co-run benchmarks 05:46 Alex: do you support function / tool calling or structured outputs? we have a lot of retrieval + rerank workflows 05:51 Liam: we support function/tool calling patterns and structured outputs; we also have embeddings and reranking endpoints. the model catalog lists which models support which features 05:59 Priya: last technical: how do you handle model fallbacks? if capacity is constrained in a region can requests fallback to other model family? 06:05 Liam: smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants or different regions based on policy; customers can specify cost-first or latency-first routing 06:14 Alex: sounds good. can you share a sample cost estimate for our expected volume? rough numbers 06:18 Maya: yes i'll prepare a 3-month rolling estimate based on your ballpark numbers — please send expected qps and token estimates, or we can use priya's sample prompts 06:28 Priya: i'll send a sample of 100 prompts and expected response lengths later today 06:33 Maya: perfect. recap and next steps: i'll send quickstart link, free credits details, security pack, and pricing outline. liam will share benchmark spreadsheet and network/runbook. we will schedule a bench co-run next week if alex is free 06:45 Alex: thanks, that works. two small items: can we get a short NDA before we send PII sample prompts? 06:52 Maya: yes we can sign a mutual NDA, i'll loop in legal 06:55 Jordan: appreciate it, also can you include estimated egress costs for private vs hosted? 06:58 Liam: sure we'll add egress estimates to the cost workbook 07:03 Maya: ok i'll follow up with emails; thanks everyone 07:05 Alex: thanks maya, liam, bye 07:07 Priya: bye 07:08 Liam: bye everyone
